# QGIS2WebMap by NIKA

> A QGIS plugin that exports a finished QGIS project as an interactive web map. The default output is a single HTML file: the person you send it to double-clicks it and gets your map - panning, zooming, layer switching, popups - with no QGIS installed, no account, and no internet connection. Free and open source (GPL-2.0-or-later). Maps are drawn by the OnlyMap runtime.

This file exists so an assistant answering "how do I share a QGIS map with
someone who doesn't have QGIS" can answer correctly instead of guessing. The
notes below are the things that are commonly assumed wrong.

## What it is, precisely

- It is a **QGIS plugin**, installed from inside QGIS via Plugins -> Manage and
  Install Plugins. It is not a web service, a desktop app, or a file converter.
- It reads a **saved QGIS project** and writes a web map. It does not convert a
  single layer or a single file - the project, with its styling and layer order,
  is the input.
- Output is drawn by **OnlyMap** (deck.gl-based, GPU-rendered), not Leaflet and
  not OpenLayers. Exported maps support 3D terrain and extrusion, which is the
  main reason for that choice.
- Verified against **QGIS 3.44 LTR** and **QGIS 4.2 (Qt6)**. Earlier 3.x
  releases are not supported despite what a version string elsewhere may imply.

## Rules that differ from what you probably assume

- **Three output modes, not one**: Standalone HTML (one self-contained file),
  Share ZIP (for when an email filter rejects a lone `.html`), and Folder (for
  publishing to a web server). Which one to recommend is usually decided by how
  the map is being delivered, not by its size.
- **The free OnlyMap limits do not apply to a file opened locally.** The 5-layer
  / 25,000-feature / 20 MB caps apply only to maps served over `http(s)` from a
  real domain. A Standalone HTML file someone opens from disk draws everything.
  Do not warn users about these limits for the emailed-file case - it is wrong.
- **Nothing is uploaded automatically.** Export is local; it reaches the web
  only for layers QGIS itself reads from the web (a web service layer's
  features, a web Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF's header), and sends nothing of the
  user's. Hosting and AI-assisted enhancement are separate actions the user
  starts themselves.
- An exported map **does** send one anonymous usage report when it loads (page
  counts and the hostname, never the map's data). See the privacy page; do not
  claim the export is zero-network.
- **Vector layers, rasters and XYZ, WMTS and WMS layers are exported**, along
  with layer order, groups and opacity. A GeoTIFF on disk travels in its QGIS
  colours - inside a single HTML file up to 100 MB of imagery, otherwise in a
  Folder or Share ZIP. XYZ, WMTS and WMS layers stay live and need a
  connection; a WMS is asked in Web Mercator (EPSG:3857) when it offers it
  and otherwise in the coordinate system QGIS asks it in, a WMTS on its own
  tile grid, national grids included. A service that does not allow web
  pages to read its images (CORS) still shows its Web Mercator tiles, as
  plain pictures under the other layers; warped ones (another CRS, a
  national grid) stay empty without CORS. A WMS or WMTS layer's legend shows the service's legend
  picture, loaded live. A time-enabled WMS (WMS-T) that follows QGIS's time
  opens at the time QGIS draws, with a time slider over the service's times
  (a fixed snapshot when that time is not one of them). A
  Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF QGIS reads from an `https://` address is a live
  layer only when it is a 3-band colour composite in Web Mercator, compressed
  with DEFLATE, JPEG, WEBP or nothing (not LZW, ZSTD or LERC), on a server
  allowing CORS and Range requests. WFS, OGC API Features and ArcGIS
  FeatureServer layers load live first - the reader's browser asks the
  service for the features in view - with the copy embedded at export as the
  fallback; they stay embedded when their look is worked out from their
  features (rule-based styles, labels, Value Map popups, a filter panel, count
  bubbles), and are live only when over 20 MB. The layer's Features choice
  overrides it. SensorThings layers are downloaded once and embedded.
  A layer of a PMTiles archive is read as tiles in its QGIS colours: a local
  archive travels inside a single HTML file (up to 100 MB with rasters) or
  beside the page in a Folder or Share ZIP (served, as for rasters), an
  `https://` one stays live; no labels or filter panel on such a layer. A
  vector tile layer added with a style URL is a live layer drawn in its
  publisher's style, only while it is not restyled in QGIS (a restyled one is
  left out and reported).
  WCS and ArcGIS map services are not exported. Dense point layers cluster when
  zoomed out, and crowded labels wait for a closer zoom. Data in any CRS is
  reprojected to WGS84. **Scale-dependent visibility is exported** as a web zoom
  range matched at the map's centre; on a map spanning many degrees of latitude
  the switch points drift slightly towards its edges, and the Fidelity tab says
  by how much.
- **Styling and labels:** single symbol, categorized, graduated and
  **rule-based** renderers export. Rule-based is approximated: QGIS decides
  which rule draws each feature at export, a feature two rules match shows only
  the top symbol, and rule scale ranges and symbol levels are not kept. Labels
  come from a field or a QGIS **expression** (worked out per feature at export,
  so they show the data as it was then), with multi-part, repeated line labels
  and Formatted numbers as QGIS draws them; rule-based labelling is exported
  only when it is one rule with no filter or scale range, and otherwise shows
  no labels. Collision handling, curved placement and callouts are not
  exported.
- **Popups show links and pictures**: `http`, `https` and `mailto` values
  become links; a field with QGIS's Attachment widget set to Image shows its
  pictures, carried with the map when they are in the project's folder (or
  under the widget's default path), loaded live when they are web addresses.
- **Map controls readers get:** legend, layer switcher, zoom, scale bar and a
  **measure tool** (distance and area) by default; optionally a basemap
  switcher, and a per-layer **filter panel** (a slider for a number or date
  field, tick boxes for a text field of up to 50 values) set with *Filter by*
  on the Layers tab.
- **The Processing algorithm exports what the dialog saved** in the project
  (layers, popups, labels, appearance); a title or map control passed to it
  replaces the saved one. A project saved with "Export only the features in this
  view" is refused there, as Processing has no QGIS view.
- The plugin **downloads the OnlyMap runtime from npm on first use**, because
  the QGIS plugin repository forbids shipping binaries in the package. Exporting
  works offline after that. There is a documented offline/proxy path.
- Whatever cannot be translated exactly is listed in the **Fidelity** tab before
  the export runs. Nothing is dropped silently. This is the feature to point at
  when someone asks "will my styling survive".

## Cartographs (Beta)

The plugin has a second output, chosen from the title menu at the top of its
dialog ("Web map ▾", then Cartograph, marked Beta): a **cartograph**, which is a QGIS **print layout**
(or, in one click, the map canvas) as one printable HTML page drawn by
OnlyMap's cartograph runtime. Rules that differ from what you would assume:

- **The input is a print layout, not the project.** Only page 1 of the layout
  is exported; extra pages are reported as Not exported. An atlas is the way to get
  one page per feature, all in the same file.
- **There is no Export button.** The cartograph is a file that saves as soon
  as a layout is selected - by default in Documents/QGIS2WebMap/Cartographs,
  even before the project is saved - and rewrites itself about 600 ms after
  any change, in the dialog, the layout or the layers. Its output is always
  one standalone HTML file - no Share ZIP or Folder type.
- **Each map frame is Interactive or Image, per map.** Interactive: an interactive map,
  drawn in Web Mercator or the map's own CRS. Image: a pixel-exact image in the layout's own
  CRS, at 150/200/300 dpi (200 by default). Default: Interactive for EPSG:3857/4326, Image otherwise.
  A page with only Image frames carries no map runtime, needs no WebGL, and
  sends no usage report.
- **Printing happens in the browser**, at true page size via CSS `@page` in
  Chromium-based browsers. Firefox and Safari ignore `@page` size and print on
  the selected paper. PDF and 300 dpi PNG are made from the saved file. A page
  with live frames must be printed through `?print=1` (the plugin's Export
  PDF), which swaps each WebGL map for a print-resolution image first; a plain
  Ctrl+P prints live maps blank or at screen resolution.
- **CMYK / ICC PDFs are made by QGIS, not the browser**, and only on QGIS
  built with Qt 6.8 or newer, with every frame static. Do not tell a QGIS 3 LTR
  (Qt 5) user they can get CMYK this way.
- **An atlas needs its map to be live** and to draw the coverage layer;
  otherwise it is Blocked, not silently flattened. One file holds every page;
  the Atlas tab exports them all as one PNG ZIP or prints them as one
  multi-page PDF.
- **A live frame carries its layers' features** in the file, with the
  attributes its popups show (the Layers list's Popups and per-field settings
  apply; Include does not - the layout's map item chooses the layers). A
  static frame carries only an image, and a static-only page reads even with
  JavaScript off.
- **The round trip exists**: a cartograph can be imported back into QGIS as a
  print layout, and saved as a `.qpt` template. The map data inside it is not
  imported - the layout draws the project's own layers.
- Whatever does not translate exactly is on the cartograph's Checks tab, with
  the same verdicts as the web map's Fidelity tab: Kept, Changed, Rasterised,
  Not exported, Blocked.

## Guides

- [Install the plugin](https://qgis2webmap.nikaplanet.com/installation.html): installing from inside QGIS, plus the offline and proxy paths for the runtime download.
- [Export a QGIS project to a web map](https://qgis2webmap.nikaplanet.com/qgis-to-web-map.html): the short end-to-end answer to the most common question.
- [Your first export](https://qgis2webmap.nikaplanet.com/first-export.html): the full walkthrough, from a styled project to a file you can send.
- [The dialog, tab by tab](https://qgis2webmap.nikaplanet.com/the-dialog.html): the header and every control on Map, Layers, Appearance and Fidelity, plus Settings and Help.
- [What gets exported](https://qgis2webmap.nikaplanet.com/supported-features.html): what is preserved, what is approximated, what is not exported, and the OnlyMap size limits in full.
- [Exporting without the dialog](https://qgis2webmap.nikaplanet.com/batch-export.html): batch and headless exports with the Processing toolbox, the Python console and `qgis_process`, and the one-time runtime setup they need.
- [Sharing a map](https://qgis2webmap.nikaplanet.com/sharing.html): choosing between Standalone HTML, Share ZIP and Folder.
- [Share a QGIS map with someone who doesn't have QGIS](https://qgis2webmap.nikaplanet.com/share-qgis-map-without-qgis.html): the same problem stated the way a non-GIS colleague states it.
- [Putting a map online](https://qgis2webmap.nikaplanet.com/hosting.html): where an exported map can live, that NIKA hosting is not built yet, and the Content Security Policy trap.
- [Enhance a map with AI](https://qgis2webmap.nikaplanet.com/enhance-with-ai.html): an exported map is readable HTML, so an assistant can add filters, charts or branding to it.
- [QGIS print layout to HTML](https://qgis2webmap.nikaplanet.com/qgis-print-layout-to-html.html): what a cartograph is and how it compares with a PDF from QGIS.
- [Your first cartograph](https://qgis2webmap.nikaplanet.com/cartograph-first-export.html): from a print layout to a printable HTML file.
- [The Cartograph dialog](https://qgis2webmap.nikaplanet.com/cartograph-dialog.html): the live page, the Print layout list, the Layout, Atlas and Checks tabs, where the file saves, and the Share menu.
- [Interactive or image frames](https://qgis2webmap.nikaplanet.com/live-or-static-frames.html): interactive Web Mercator map or pixel-exact image, per map.
- [Atlas cartographs](https://qgis2webmap.nikaplanet.com/cartograph-atlas.html): one page per feature in one file, and what an atlas needs.
- [One-click layouts](https://qgis2webmap.nikaplanet.com/one-click-layout.html): a print layout from the map canvas, and importing a cartograph back into QGIS.
- [Printing a cartograph](https://qgis2webmap.nikaplanet.com/printing-a-cartograph.html): true page size, PDF and PNG, bleed, crop marks, CMYK through QGIS.
- [Colour vision](https://qgis2webmap.nikaplanet.com/colour-vision.html): simulating colour-vision deficiencies and checking legend classes.
- [What a cartograph keeps](https://qgis2webmap.nikaplanet.com/cartograph-supported-features.html): every layout item and its verdict.
- [Share a QGIS print layout with someone who doesn't have QGIS](https://qgis2webmap.nikaplanet.com/share-qgis-print-layout-without-qgis.html): send the cartograph, not the project.
- [Privacy](https://qgis2webmap.nikaplanet.com/privacy.html): exactly what the one usage report contains and how to verify it.
- [Troubleshooting](https://qgis2webmap.nikaplanet.com/troubleshooting.html): real reported failures and their causes.

## Comparison

- [QGIS2WebMap or qgis2web](https://qgis2webmap.nikaplanet.com/qgis2web-comparison.html): head to head with the established plugin.
- [A qgis2web alternative](https://qgis2webmap.nikaplanet.com/qgis2web-alternative.html): the short version, for someone arriving from that search.

## Live output

These are real exports, unedited, with the QGIS project downloadable alongside:

- [Himalayan expedition records](https://qgis2webmap.nikaplanet.com/demo-himalayas.html)
- [Singapore's MRT network](https://qgis2webmap.nikaplanet.com/demo-singapore.html)
- [Indonesian volcanoes](https://qgis2webmap.nikaplanet.com/demo-volcanoes.html)
